newsitem.title: FRANCE: GEC Alsthom says approached Westinghouse, no talks.
newsitem.headline: GEC Alsthom says approached Westinghouse, no talks.

text.p: Franco-British joint venture GEC Alsthom said in reaction to a French press report that it had expressed an interest in Westinghouse's Power Generation business.
But Westinghouse had not followed up and no talks had been started on the matter, GEC Alsthom said in a statement after the report in French daily Liberation.

It said France's Framatome was interested in the nuclear side of the Westinghouse energy business and that this "bolsters the prospects for the two French groups and the French industry in this affair".
"It is true GEC Alsthom expressed an interest in buying Westinghouse's Power Generation business," said the statement.
"But to this day Westinghouse has not followed up and no negotiations have been started," it said.

"The fact of Framatome having an interest in the Energy Systems (nuclear) business is something which would enhance prospects for the two French groups and the French industry in this affair," it added.
GEC Alsthom said the document referred to in the Liberation report was "an internal working document, a preliminary to contact with Westinghouse".

The group also said: "It is totally out of the question that the treasury of one of the two firms (GEC Alsthom or Framatome) be used for the benefit of the other," referring to Liberation's report that GEC Alsthom would tap state-owned Framatome's treasury in such a deal.
Earlier, Framatome denied formally a newspaper report saying it was preparing a bid for Westinghouse Electric Corp energy division.
"Framatome denies formally a newspaper article saying it is preparing a bid for a Westinghouse unit," Philippe Raulin, the company's secretary-general, told Reuters.
GEC Alsthom is a joint-venture of Alcatel Alsthom and GEC Plc.
Alcatel also has a 44 percent stake in Framatome, the rest being controlled by French state entities.
